questionTextEn: Which of the following is the characteristic tool of the Acheulean industry?
explanationEn: The Acheulean Industry is characterised by symmetrical bifacial handaxes and cleavers, belonging to the Lower Palaeolithic period. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)
subject: History

questionTextEn: The Levallois technique (prepared core method) is associated with which period?
explanationEn: The Levallois Technique belongs to the Middle Palaeolithic period, NOT Lower Palaeolithic. This is a common prelims trap. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Which site in the Belan Valley (Vindhyas) is significant because it shows a complete sequence of all Stone Age phases?
explanationEn: On the northern spurs of the Vindhyas in the Belan Valley, all three phases of the Palaeolithic followed by the Mesolithic and then the Neolithic have been found in sequence — a complete Stone Age sequence at one location. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Microliths are the hallmark tools of which period?
explanationEn: Microliths (small stone tools) are the hallmark and characteristic tools of the Mesolithic period. The Mesolithic Age in India started about 8000 B.C. and continued up to about 4000 B.C. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Which is the largest Mesolithic site in India?
explanationEn: Bagor in Rajasthan is the largest Mesolithic site in India. Note: Bagor is a Mesolithic site, NOT Neolithic — this is a common exam trap. (Source: Standard references)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Which was probably the first animal to be domesticated by humans?
explanationEn: Dog was probably the first animal to be tamed. (Source: NCERT Class 6, Our Pasts-I, Ch.2)
subject: History

questionTextEn: At Burzahom (Kashmir), what unique burial practice was observed that is not found elsewhere in India?
optionBEn: Domestic dogs were buried with their masters in graves
explanationEn: At Burzahom, domestic dogs were buried with their masters in graves — a unique practice not found elsewhere in India. People lived in pit dwellings and used coarse grey pottery. Earliest date approximately 2400 B.C. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Which site provides the earliest evidence of farming in the Indian subcontinent?
explanationEn: Mehrgarh in Balochistan (Pakistan) provides the earliest evidence of farming in the Indian subcontinent, with barley and wheat cultivation, square/rectangular houses with compartments, and burials with goats. (Source: NCERT Class 6, Our Pasts-I)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Evidence of rice cultivation in the Neolithic period has been found at which site?
explanationEn: Evidence of rice cultivation has been found at Koldihwa in Uttar Pradesh. (Source: Standard references)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Which site on the banks of the river Narmada has yielded the maximum number of cereals found at any single site in India?
explanationEn: Navdatoli on the Narmada bank yielded the maximum variety of cereals — wheat, rice, lentil (masur), black gram, green gram, grass pea, ber and linseed. Perhaps no other place in India has so many cereals discovered. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India, Ch.5)
subject: History

questionTextEn: The Chalcolithic culture of Kayatha is located in which state?
explanationEn: Kayatha is located in western Madhya Pradesh, NOT Gujarat — this is a common exam trap. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Black-and-Red Ware pottery is the distinctive marker of which period?
explanationEn: Black-and-Red Ware pottery — thrown on wheel, occasionally painted with white linear designs — is the distinctive marker of the Chalcolithic period. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India, Ch.5)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Chirand, which yielded considerable bone implements in a late neolithic setup, is located on the banks of which river?
explanationEn: Chirand is located about 40 km west of Patna, on the Ganga. It is the only other place (besides Burzahom) yielding considerable bone implements in a late neolithic setup. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)
subject: History

questionTextEn: What were the main crops cultivated in the southern Indian Neolithic sites according to R.S. Sharma?
explanationEn: In south Indian Neolithic sites (Maski, Brahmagiri, Hallur, Tekkalakota in Karnataka, and Paiyampalli in Tamil Nadu), people cultivated ragi and horse gram (kulithi). (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)
subject: History

questionTextEn: Evidence of the use of fire in prehistoric India has been found at which site?
explanationEn: Evidence of fire use (traces of ash) has been found at Kurnool Caves in Andhra Pradesh, associated with the Upper Palaeolithic period. (Source: R.S. Sharma, Ancient India)
subject: History
